subject: WebSocket multiplexing pilot — concurrency & rate handoff
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
To: Evan Cho <evan.cho@brightware.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: 2029-05-10T14:02:00Z
Subject: WebSocket multiplexing pilot — concurrency & rate handoff

Hey Evan —

Great to talk earlier. Quick recap from our discovery focused on performance/SLOs and next steps for a short pilot so your engineering team can validate WebSocket + multiplexed connections with Redwood. I captured the items we agreed on (notes + asks below) and a proposed temporary rate/quota handoff so you can exercise realistic load patterns.

Call highlights (TL;DR):
- Primary integration: bi-directional WebSocket endpoints using connection multiplexing (single TCP with many logical channels).
- SLO targets: 95th p95 latencies <= 120ms for streaming tokens, p99 tail <= 350ms for 1–2k token responses.
- Throughput: sustained ~18k tokens/min baseline, with short spikes to 45k tokens/min (1–3 minute windows).
- Concurrency: anticipate ~750 concurrent logical request streams (many fan-in on a few sockets). Peak simultaneous active requests ~1,200 during batch publish spikes.
- Connection expectations: client will keep ~40 persistent sockets from the same origin; each socket multiplexes up to ~50 concurrent streams.
- Persistence/keepalive: long-lived sockets (hours), occasional reconnects on deploys.

Requested next steps from BrightWare:
1) Confirm the pilot window (we proposed 2 weeks starting next Mon).
2) Share a small test harness or traffic replay that mimics your token profile (we attached a template CSV).
3) Provide a test subdomain and firewall allowlist so we can route test traffic.

Proposed temporary quota handoff (for pilot only):
- Base QPS: 300 requests/sec aggregated across sockets (sustained).
- Concurrent logical streams: 900 guaranteed, 1,400 burst.
- Token throughput: 60,000 tokens/min sustained cap for pilot, with 90,000 tokens/min burst (1–3 mins) to observe degradation characteristics.
- Per-socket multiplexing: allow up to 60 streams/socket for pilot to mirror your client.
- Streaming sessions: streaming output enabled; per-token latency traced and exported to the pilot dashboard.

Attachments: redwood-slo-conn-summary.pdf (contains SLO definitions and pilot instrumentation checklist), pilot-metrics-template.csv (a short CSV you can use to replay token sizes/time).

If that aligns, I can push the pilot quotas to your account and loop in Marissa (solutions eng) to kick off onboarding and the tracing hooks.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya — really helpful summary. Confirm a few items from our side:

1) Pilot window: can start Tue 2029-05-14 for two weeks (preferred).
2) Concurrency specifics: our internal telemetry expects ~700 active logical streams during normal peak and up to 1,250 during batch deliveries. The 1,400 burst you proposed is fine for short windows but can we prioritize sustained guarantees around 900?
3) Multiplexing: we expect 30–50 streams/socket; most clients will be at ~32 streams/socket.
4) Tokens: our median response size is ~90 tokens, 95th ~420 tokens. We will attach a sample of realistic traces; the CSV template is perfect.

Two asks before you flip any quotas on:
- Can you provide a simple error-mode doc: how Redwood surfaces backpressure or dropped streams under saturation? (we need to map to client-side retry/backoff).
- Do you have a quick table of per-request pricing estimate for streaming vs non-streaming token units for the pilot period? We want to budget the pilot spend.

Looping in infra@brightware.ai for the test subdomain follow-up.

Evan
Principal Engineer, BrightWare
ev an.cho@brightware.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
To: Evan Cho <evan.cho@brightware.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: 2029-05-10T19:03:00Z
Subject: Re: WebSocket multiplexing pilot — concurrency & rate handoff

Appreciate the fast turn, Evan — all good. Quick responses below and next steps: 

- Pilot start: Tue 2029-05-14 confirmed. I'll schedule a 30m kickoff with Marissa to walk through the instrumentation and sample traces.
- Sustained guarantees: we will lock in 900 concurrent logical streams as the guaranteed floor for the pilot, with the 1,400 burst cap for short peaks. I'll note this in the pilot configuration.
- Error/backpressure behavior: short doc below (we'll add a full FAQ to the Drive link):
  * When the serving pool is saturated, Redwood returns a 429 with a Retry-After header for non-streaming requests.
  * For streaming sessions that exceed per-stream CPU/kv-cache limits, we may deliver an end-of-stream message with code 410 and a brief reason string ("session-throttled").
  * Multiplexed socket-level backpressure: if the socket's multiplex queue is full, Redwood will start to reject new logical streams with 503 ("socket-overloaded") and a Retry-After.
  * Tracing: every 429/503/410 emits a structured log event that appears in the pilot dashboard so you can map client behavior to server-side signals.

- Pricing sketch for pilot: (estimates — final bill per contract)
  * Streaming tokens: $0.0018 per token for pilot test account (metered per emitted token).
  * Non-streaming (sync) tokens: $0.0021 per token.
  * Connection surcharge: $0.03 per persistent socket/hour over 30 sockets during pilot (to capture long-lived socket resource use).
  * Note: we can apply a one-time pilot credit up to $2,500 on request — I'll escalate if you want that added.

Next immediate actions:
- I will create the pilot configuration and enable the quotas on your test account by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa will send a short onboarding checklist and invite for Tue kickoff.
- Please send the sample traces and test subdomain to infra@brightware.ai and CC our team.

Putting Marissa and Ben on this thread so they have the context.

Best,
Aditya

Hi Evan — quick logistics note from the solutions side before kickoff: 

1) Instrumentation checklist (short):
   - Enable debug tracing header X-Redwood-Trace on test requests.
   - Emit per-stream ID in the payload so we can correlate multiplexed channels back to logical requests.
   - Push the sample CSV to the Drive link and name it brightware-traces-20290510.csv.

2) Pilot dashboard & alerts:
   - We'll create a pilot dashboard (read-only) and invite infra@brightware.ai. It will show p50/p95/p99 token latency, concurrent_streams, socket_count, and 429/503 event rates.
   - We'll add an alert for 429 rate > 0.5% sustained over 60s so we can triage quickly.

3) Quick test plan for Tue kickoff (30m):
   - 0–5m: confirm test subdomain and allowlist.
   - 5–15m: run a 10m steady-state at 18k tokens/min.
   - 15–25m: run three 2m spike windows to 45k tokens/min.
   - 25–30m: review traces and validate tracing headers.

If you want, we can also enable a limited dedicated pool for the pilot (extra $/hour) to reduce noise from other tenants; Ben can follow up with a quick pricing delta.

See you Tue —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference
